title: Accelerating Advanced Light Source Science Through Multi-Facility HPC Workflows
problem: Synchrotron beamlines produce high-volume, complex data requiring CPU and GPU algorithms for 3D reconstruction; scientists need seamless access to HPC resources (ALCF, NERSC) without direct backend system access for real-time feedback.
motivation: Beamline scientists need rapid feedback on data quality (microtomography) and high-quality reconstructions for deeper analysis. Remote HPC integration enables leveraging cutting-edge compute resources without local infrastructure.
method: Infrastructure connecting ALS synchrotron to HPC centers via ESnet. Two workflows: (1) Real-time streaming to NERSC compute nodes for on-the-fly reconstruction; (2) Automated file transfer to NERSC/ALCF for intensive 3D reconstruction. CPU and GPU algorithms deployed.
key_novelty: Multi-facility workflow architecture streaming synchrotron data to HPC for transparent algorithm deployment; dual pipeline (streaming for rapid feedback, batch for quality).
contributions: Real-time data streaming pipeline delivering reconstruction feedback <10 seconds
File-based workflow producing high-quality reconstructions in 20-30 minutes
Transparent HPC resource access for beamline users without direct backend access
CPU and GPU algorithm deployment infrastructure
Plans for extension to additional beamlines
limitations: Limited to ALS currently; extension timeline unclear
Performance details sparse (throughput, GPU utilization, cost)
No cost/benefit analysis of streaming vs file-based approaches
Abstract-only prevents evaluation of algorithm choices
primary_theme: Multi-facility synchrotron data processing via HPC
